threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused when the bus driver shouts 'next stop, Clapton' like it's a riddle instead of directions. Classic rookie move.
Last night on the 196, saw a guy serenading a couple with a ukulele. Best free concert ever, but the couple looked mortified.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw my neighbor's pet chicken roaming the street while I was waiting for the bus – that's when I knew Neukölln had truly claimed me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop that doubles as a gallery and hosts poetry nights. Where else can you munch on döner while soaking in art?

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they swap out their BART plans for a 10-minute walk after hearing about last night's Civic Center chaos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 at almost midnight last night—driver cracked jokes with riders while navigating Tenderloin's potholes. That's the spirit!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think the fountains in Plaça del Sol are for decoration, not realizing locals fill their water bottles there daily. It’s a community staple.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by their bewilderment at 'tapas' time—dining at 6 PM and expecting it to be full. Just a few locals there, enjoying the quiet.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the ‘Overground’ instead of just the ‘Gooner Train’ when talking to locals. Definitely a newcomer mistake.
Last night on the 35, a guy on crutches tried to steal a seat from a sleeping tourist. The tourist woke up confused, just saw the crutches.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a wedding party parading down the street with a vintage Trabant, music blaring, and everyone dancing was when I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a karaoke bar in an old U-Bahn tunnel – it’s got the best acoustics and a vibe like no other.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they know the hidden corners of Dolores Park and avoid the BART fiasco like a pro, especially after a late match.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Heard a guy on the 14 Mission just casually explain the concept of 'transit equity' to a tourist. Only in SF would that kind of conversation happen on a bus.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just quiet streets and plazas, but they miss the pulse of locals in late-night bars, where the real stories get shared.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the maps they constantly whip out, trying to navigate the ever-changing bus routes like it's their first day.
